Chief Inspector.

The Local Rice Situation

SOMETHING has got to be done about the rice situation here and done quickly. It is rapidly getting out of control and if the authorities of the foreign areas do not take immediate action in tackling the problem, its further deterioration will certainly lead to a crisis the like of which Shanghai has not faced.

Far be it from our desire to spread alarm. But the question has become increasingly important. Half-hearted measures to curb profiteering have failed miserably. More effective means must be sought to combat the situation

Most foreigners have vague ideas as to how important rice is to the Chinese. They seem to think that rice to the average Chinese is what bread is to the average foreigner. In a sense, it is true. But because the average foreigner eats meat and vegetables on account of his higher income, he can go fairly well without much bread, whereas the average Chinese, not being in a position to afford even a sufficient supply of vegetables, depends on rice for the main source of his energy.

THE price of the native rice was $14 per shih (picul) two years ago, but it is now over $90. Very soon, if no radical steps are taken by the powers that be, it will go over the $100 mark. Saigon rice is slightly cheaper but its prices have kept in step with those of the native rice.

According to the Chinese cost of living index for September released by the Shanghai Municipal Council, rice stocks of the Saigon variety are plentiful here. Saigon rice is what is being generally consumed by the Chinese working class, and there are ample stocks in local godowns to last several months. There is no shortage to be feared, for the present at least, and there is no reason why prices should go up from day to day.

The soaring of the prices can be traced to hoarding and profiteering. Yielding to the lust for gold, the dealers capitalize on rumors of political situations, fluctuations in foreign exchange, and even weather conditions. In fact, a good portion of the rumors was started by the dealers themselves so that they could reap handsome profits and in most cases they did. Then there is the small group of what is called middlemen who seem to hold a monopoly of handling the distribution of rice bought by foreign importers and taking a good cut at the profit.

WHILE the dealers and middlemen are getting fabulously rich, the Chinese masses in this city are at their wits' end in their efforts to get enough rice for their families. The scenes of the poor class of people jamming in a long queue to get a dollar's worth of "cheap" rice at the allotted "cheap" sales are nothing short of pathetic. And what each gets, if he succeeds in getting it, is just about sufficient to feed three persons for one meal!

There have been a few isolated cases where dealers and shopkeepers were prosecuted by the Shanghai Municipal Council for profiteering, but they helped little, if any, in curbing the increases of the rice prices.

More drastic measures are urgently needed against hoarding and profiteering and Council authorities in both the Settlement and Concession must put their foot down in helping solve a difficult problem that threatens the city with grave consequences. They should also give careful consideration to the suggestion made by Mr. John Ahlers of the Shanghai Evening Post and see if they can give their aid toward its realization. Mr. Ahlers's proposal calls for a big combine of local industrial interests to import the whole of rice required for Shanghai's industrial workers and working class Chinese in this city. We ourselves believe that the project is one of the ways to combat profiteering and it is well worth undertaking.
pages.zh:
本地米市状况

必须对这里的米市状况采取行动，且须迅速行动。局势正迅速失控，如果租界当局不立即着手解决这一问题，其进一步恶化必将导致上海从未面临过的危机。

我们绝非有意散布恐慌。但这个问题已变得日益重要。遏制囤积居奇的半吊子措施已彻底失败。必须寻求更有效的手段来应对这一局面。

大多数外国人对大米对中国人的重要性只有模糊的概念。他们似乎认为，大米对普通中国人而言，就像面包对普通外国人一样。从某种意义上说，这没错。但由于普通外国人收入较高，食用肉类和蔬菜，因此即使少吃面包也能过得去；而普通中国人甚至无力购买充足的蔬菜，主要依赖大米作为能量来源。

两年前，国产米的价格为每石（担）14元，但现在已超过90元。如果当权者不采取根本性措施，很快价格就将突破100元大关。西贡米稍便宜一些，但其价格一直与国产米同步上涨。

根据上海市参议会发布的9月份中国居民生活指数，本地西贡米库存充足。西贡米是中国工人阶级普遍食用的米种，本地仓库中有足够的库存可供数月之需。至少目前不必担心短缺，也没有理由让价格日复一日地上涨。

价格飙升可归因于囤积和投机倒把。受贪欲驱使，商人利用政治局势、外汇波动甚至天气状况的谣言牟利。事实上，相当一部分谣言是由商人自己散布的，以便从中获取丰厚利润，而在大多数情况下他们也确实做到了。此外，还有一小群所谓的中间人，他们似乎垄断了外国进口商所购大米的分销渠道，并从中截取高额利润。

当商人和中间人变得极其富有时，本市的中国民众却在为家人筹集足够的大米而绞尽脑汁。贫困阶层排起长队，只为在指定的“平价”销售点买到价值一元的“廉价”米，这种场景简直令人心酸。而且，即使成功买到，每人所得也仅够三人吃一顿饭！

曾有个别案例显示，上海市参议会起诉了一些投机倒把的商人和店主，但这些举措对遏制米价上涨几乎没有任何帮助。

亟需采取更严厉的措施来打击囤积和投机行为，公共租界和法租界的当局必须下定决心，协助解决这个可能给城市带来严重后果的棘手问题。他们还应认真考虑《上海晚邮报》约翰·阿勒斯（John Ahlers）先生提出的建议，看看能否提供帮助以实现该建议。阿勒斯先生的提议呼吁本地工业界联合起来，进口上海产业工人和本市中国工人阶级所需的全部大米。我们自己认为，该项目是对抗投机倒把的途径之一，非常值得实施。

bags.

食品

Municipal Council has revised its

cipate in the rice allowance.

pages.en:
0999.

Japan Reported Facing
Rice Shortage
Difference to Be Imported :
"No Cause for Alarm"

Tokyo, Oct. 4.
The Ministry of Agriculture's first
official estimate of this year's rice
crop in Japan disclosed that the
nation is facing a severe shortage of
the staple Japanese food
The forecast, based on figures
available on September 20, estimated
that the rice crop would total 63,119,-
430 kokus. This represents a sharp
drop of 5,806,459 kokus from the
actual crop in 1939.
The Agriculture Ministry announced
that the severe rice shortage would
be met by importing rice from abroad.
Consequently, the announcement said,
there is no cause for alarm.
The "Asahi Shimbun" reported,
however, that present restrictions on
rice consumption in Japan undoubted-
ly would be stiffened.—United Press.
pages.zh:
0999.

据报道日本面临
大米短缺
差额将通过进口弥补：
“无需惊慌”

东京，10月4日电。
日本农业部今年水稻收成的首次官方估算显示，该国正面临主食严重短缺的局面。

该预测基于9月20日的数据，估计水稻总产量为63,119,430石（kokus）。这比1939年的实际产量大幅减少了5,806,459石。

农业部宣布，将通过从国外进口大米来弥补严重的大米短缺。因此，公告称，无需惊慌。

然而，《朝日新闻》报道说，日本目前的大米消费限制无疑将会加强。——合众社。

pages.en:
Famine In North
Flour Situation Precarious
Despite Rumored Imports
(Havas)

TIENTSIN, Feb 27.—The
flour situation in North China
remains precarious and the
danger of a shortage of this
commodity has by no means
been removed despite shipments
of more than 1,000,000 bags
from Australia and Japan.
Average requirements of the
urban population are estimated
at 1,000,000 bags per month
for every 300,000 families.
Prices are still soaring, even
though the American flour export
subsidy has been raised from 15
cents to $1.40 U.S. currency per
barrel. Higher prices are due
partly to the recent drop in the
local currency and to an increase
in flour prices abroad as a result
of the European War.

Link-System Exchange
While about 26 per cent is
gained by importing flour on
the export-import link system
prevalent in North China since
the introduction of exchange
control the amount of foreign
currency released by exports
and available under this link
system is insufficient due to the

considerable reduction of exports
to non-Yen bloc countries.
Various embargo regulations,
transport difficulties, and cutting-
off of a number of supply sources
in the interior due to the hostili-
ties, are also to be held responsible
for the reduction of available for-
eign currency.

With a shortage of flour in North
China now declared to be “im-
minent” and as prices have reached
the $30 mark per bag measures to
curb speculation and profiteering
have had to be enforced by the
French and British authorities in
Tientsin.

Sales Started
Whilst the French Concession has
started sale of flour at $15
per bag the British Muni-
cipal Council has enforced
agency control measures and
has ordered the registration of
flour stocks in the Concession. This
has caused the price of flour to go
down to $15.50 within the Conces-
sion, seemingly in anticipation of
price control measures.

A few cases of flour-rioting and
looting of flour lorries and shops
recently occurred in the native city,
but the situation in the French and
British Concessions is calm.
pages.zh:
北方饥荒
面粉形势岌岌可危
尽管有进口传闻
（哈瓦斯社）

天津，2月27日电。—华北的面粉形势依然岌岌可危，尽管已从澳大利亚和日本运入超过1,000,000袋，但这种商品短缺的危险远未消除。

据估计，城市人口的平均需求量为每30万户家庭每月1,000,000袋。

尽管美国面粉出口补贴已从每桶15美分提高到1.40美元（美金），但价格仍在飙升。价格上涨部分原因是近期本地货币贬值，以及由于欧洲战争导致国外面粉价格上涨。

联系汇率制度

虽然自实行外汇管制以来，通过在华北盛行的进出口联系制度进口面粉可获得约26%的收益，但由于对非日元集团国家出口的显著减少，通过出口释放并在此联系制度下可用的外币数量不足。

各种禁运法规、运输困难，以及因敌对行动导致内地许多供应来源被切断，也是造成可用外币减少的原因。

鉴于华北面粉短缺现在被宣布为“迫在眉睫”，且价格已达到每袋30美元的水平，天津的法英当局不得不强制执行遏制投机和囤积居奇的措施。

开始销售

虽然法租界已开始以每袋15元的价格出售面粉，但工部局已实施代理控制措施，并命令登记租界内的面粉库存。这使得租界内的面粉价格降至15.50元，似乎是在预期价格管制措施。

最近在华界发生了几起面粉骚乱以及抢劫面粉卡车和商店的事件，但法租界和公共租界的局势平静。

SMC Chinese Staff

The Rice Allowance authorised

市参议会华籍职员
获得大米津贴

市参议会授权向月薪100元及以下、名单列于各部门月度工资单上且未享受膳食补助的华籍雇员发放大米津贴。1月和2月的津贴分别定为3.37元和3.67元。

pages.en:
Flour And Wheat

The unofficial rate of native flour weak-
ened yesterday as outport and interior
dealers were reluctant to buy in view
of the sale of 7,500 bags to retail shops
for cheap sale.
As a large shipment of foreign wheat
was reported en route to Shanghai, local
dealers and mills awaited developments.
As a result the rate registered a loss
of $0.20 per bag, with Japanese merchants
absorbing six carloads of Soochow wheat
at $25.60 per bag.
pages.zh:
面粉与小麦

昨日国产面粉的非官方汇率走弱，因为外地和内地商人鉴于有7,500袋面粉出售给零售店进行平价销售，不愿买入。

据报道，大批外国小麦正在运往上海的途中，本地商人和磨坊主都在观望事态发展。结果，价格每袋下跌0.20元，日本商人以每袋25.60元的价格吸收了六车皮苏州小麦。

pages.en:
Profiteers In
Rice Jailed
For 15 Days

Yet another sequel to the mount-
ing cost of rice in the city was
heard in the First Special District
Court yesterday, when two rice
shop employees were sentenced to
jail terms for selling the cereal at
above the official price limits and
four loafers were imprisoned for
participating in a "rice riot"

Although the owner was still
at large, two employees of the
Tch San Rice Hong of 68 Honan
Road were each sentenced to 15
days' imprisonment for selling
rice at more than $56 per picul.
Giving their names as Li Shan-
kan, accountant and Kuo Ming-
teh, apprentice, the prisoners were
arrested at the Honan Road ad-
dress Wednesday afternoon on a
complaint filed by a customer of the
establishment

Official Limit Exceeded

The complainant who appeared
as witness stated that he had to
pay $50 for a picul of rice at the
rice hong His testimony was cor-
roborated by entries into the hong's
daily ledger which was produced in
court as evidence

The four loafers who were
also sentenced rushed the Shing
Shan Rice Hong on Tsu Ka
Toon Road near Alcock Road on
Wednesday.
In company with about 20 peo-
ple the accused were said to have
made away with about ten bags of
rice valued at $750

Rice Shop Victimized

The riot occurred at about 1
o'clock in the afternoon when
the street was crowded with
shoppers and pedestrians. After
forcing their way into the rice
shops, the prisoners and their
accomplices helped themselves
to the stock of the establish-
ment
Police answering an alarm
raised by a shop apprentice
arrived on the scene after the
prisoners had carried away the
cereal. In a subsequent search
of the neighborhood, the prison-
ers were found in a nearby alley.
The prisoners gave their names
as Wang King-seng, Siao Po-keng
Hsieh Ah-nam and Chao Siao-sz
They were found in possession of
some rice when they were appre-
hended by police
pages.zh:
米商牟取暴利
被判监禁十五日

昨日，第一特区法院审理了又一起因本市米价不断上涨而引发的案件，两名米店雇员因以高于官方限价的价格出售大米而被判处监禁，四名无业游民因参与“米骚乱”而被投入监狱。

尽管店主仍然在逃，但河南路68号“德三米号”（Tch San Rice Hong）的两名雇员因以每石超过56元的价格出售大米，各被判处15天监禁。这两名囚犯自称李山坎（Li Shan-kan，会计）和郭明德（Kuo Ming-teh，学徒），他们是在周三下午根据该店一名顾客的投诉，在河南路地址被捕的。

超出官方限价

作为证人出庭的投诉人陈述，他在该米号购买一石大米不得不支付50元。他的证词得到了米号日常账簿记录的佐证，该账簿已作为证据提交法庭。

另外四名同样被判刑的无业游民于周三冲击了位于阿尔科克路（Alcock Road）附近朱家屯路（Tsu Ka Toon Road）的“兴山米号”（Shing Shan Rice Hong）。
据称，被告与约20人一起抢走了价值750美元的约十袋大米。

米店受害

骚乱发生在下午1点左右，当时街道上挤满了购物者和行人。在强行闯入米店后，囚犯及其同伙肆意拿取店内的存货。
警方接到一名店学徒发出的警报后赶到现场，此时囚犯们已携粮逃离。在随后对附近的搜查中，警方在附近的一条弄堂里发现了这些囚犯。
囚犯自报姓名为王金生（Wang King-seng）、萧伯庚（Siao Po-keng）、谢阿南（Hsieh Ah-nam）和赵小四（Chao Siao-sz）。他们在被警方逮捕时，身上搜出了一些大米。

pages.en:
Four Rice Rioters in
District Court

Charged with Having
Stolen Four Piculs

Four alleged rice rioters, one of
them a woman, were brought before
the First Special District Court yes-
terday on a writ of detention. They
admitted having taken part in the
riot in a rice shop in Point Road near
East Yuhang Road on Wednesday but
implicated a factory worker in East
Yuhang Road as their ringleader.
They were remanded for one week.
Scores of men and women stormed
into the rice shop on Wednesday
afternoon and looted the premises of
four piculs of rice. The stolen rice was
alleged to have been taken by the
factory workers. The mob was later
dispersed by the police.
Two other rice dealers were each
sentenced to fifteen days' imprison-
ment yesterday by the same court for
selling their rice beyond the official
price of $40 a picul. A customer
bought a picul of rice from their shop
by paying $50 but in the bill of sale
only $40 was mentioned. An argu-
ment between the seller and buyer
aroused the attention of the police
resulting in the accused being arrested.
Fifteen men and women were
arrested but not charged, as it was
alleged that they had bought flour
from the officially sponsored flour
cheap sale shops and re-sold them for
making profit. Since it was difficult
to find evidence against the fraudulent
dealings they have now been released
without being referred to the Court.
Meanwhile, another broken Saigon
rice cheap sale movement will be
started today under the auspices of
the Shanghai Rice Distribution Com-
mittee which recently distributed
about 20,000 bags of the rice to the
poor at a very cheap price. As in the
former case, a person is allowed to
buy only $1 worth of the grain today,
and the quantity is somewhat reduced
as compared with the first sale.
pages.zh:
四名米骚乱分子
出庭受审

被控盗窃四石大米

昨日，四名涉嫌参与米骚乱者（其中一人为女性）被拘票传唤至第一特区法院。他们承认参与了周三在东余杭路附近波因特路（Point Road）一家米店的骚乱，但指认东余杭路的一名工厂工人为其头目。他们被还押候审一周。
周三下午，数十名男女冲进该米店，洗劫了四石大米。据称，被盗大米由工厂工人拿走。暴民后来被警察驱散。
昨日，同一家法院还判处另外两名米商各监禁十五天，原因是他们出售大米的价格超过了每石40元的官方定价。一名顾客在该店购买一石大米支付了50元，但售货单据上只写了40元。买卖双方的争吵引起了警方的注意，导致被告被捕。
另有十五名男女被捕但未被起诉，据称他们从官方赞助的平价面粉店购买面粉后转售牟利。由于难以找到针对这种欺诈行为的证据，他们现已获释，未被移送法院。
与此同时，在上海米粮分配委员会的主持下，另一轮碎西贡米平价销售活动将于今日开始。该委员会最近以极低的价格向穷人分发了约2万袋此类大米。与前一次一样，今日每人仅限购买价值1元的大米，且数量较第一次销售有所减少。

pages.en:
Carb Profiteering

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS.

SIR,—Apart from the elite circle of gilt-edged, gold-salaried "privy boys" of Shanghai big business—and they are only a handful—millions of people here, both foreign and Chinese, are suffering acute distress, owing to the outrageous profiteering which has been permitted in the Settlement and Concession.

Articles by the foreign and Chinese press have shown beyond all doubt that there is profiteering that inflated commodity prices are not entirely due to Japanese and Japan-inspired taxes and tariffs.

Large stocks of rice, flour and coal are being held in godowns, beef and mutton imports are being restricted by both finance and stall-holders—the former to cornering Hongkew Market, and the latter to keep prices high. Vegetables which may be bought for ten to five cents a pound direct from the farmer, are from twice to four times the price when sold over counters in the city.

The Shanghai Municipal Council has on previous occasions exercised extraordinary powers to meet emergencies. The city has been turned into an armed camp, not so much to protect a starving multitude, but it is submitted, Shanghai is faced with a very real emergency, with the prospect of riot and looting unless something is done to prevent it.

Let the Shanghai Municipal Council exert its fullest powers, seize all hoarded stocks, pay for them at fixed prices and release the goods to the public. If this were done I am quite certain, humanity alone would take an immediate and remedial step.

Yours, &c.,
A READER.

Shanghai, Jan. 20, 1938.
pages.zh:
煤炭牟取暴利

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——除了上海大企业中那些享有高薪、地位显赫的少数“亲信”圈子外，这里数百万中外民众正遭受着极大的痛苦，这是由于租界和法租界内允许的猖獗投机倒把行为所致。

中外报刊的文章已毫无疑问地表明，存在投机倒把行为，商品价格的膨胀并不完全归因于日本及受日本影响的税收和关税。

大量的大米、面粉和煤炭被囤积在仓库中，牛肉和羊肉的进口受到金融家和摊位持有者的限制——前者旨在垄断虹口市场，后者旨在维持高价。直接从农民手中以每磅五至十美分购买的蔬菜，在城市柜台出售时价格却翻了两到四倍。

上海公共租界工部局此前曾行使特别权力以应对紧急情况。城市已变成一座武装营地，但这并非主要是为了保护饥饿的大众，而是必须指出，上海正面临非常真实的紧急状况，除非采取措施加以预防，否则将面临骚乱和抢劫的前景。

让上海公共租界工部局行使其全部权力，没收所有囤积的物资，按固定价格付款，并向公众发放这些货物。如果这样做，我确信，仅凭人道主义就会立即采取补救措施。

此致，
一名读者

上海，1938年1月20日。

pages.en:
Living Cost Here Soaring To
New High, Council Reports

Unprecedented increases in the cost of living in Shanghai were registered in January, according to a report issued yesterday by the Industrial Section of the Shanghai Municipal Council.

Based upon a survey conducted among the city's workers, the report found that while commodity prices increased to 325 per cent higher than those of 1926 the purchasing power of the Chinese dollar declined by slightly more than 30 cents.

As compared with the previous month, prices in January showed a flat increase, averaging from 10 per cent to more than 100 per cent, it was reported.

Of all the commodities vegetables showed the greatest increase in price. Green vegetables were raised as much as 103 per cent over the December quotation. Spinach rose 81 per cent and soya bean bread and turnip rose over 45 per cent.

Meat Prices Soar

Meat, fish and poultry also showed significant rises varying from about 7 per cent in the case of fresh pork to 26 per cent in the case of fresh fish.

Soya bean oil and pork lard declined about 10 per cent being the exception of their spectacular rise during the preceding month.

Although the price of rice remained fairly constant, according to the report, ranging from $37 to $39 per shih, the price of flour was up from $8.60 per bag to more than $10.

Bean curd a foodstuff widely used by workers, cost considerably higher in January than in December, fried bean curd being quoted at 65 cents per piece in December while in January it cost 80 per chin.

Rental Goes Up

Rental took another jump in January, according to the survey, rising nearly 10 per cent as compared with the index for December. Workers had to pay for instance, $6.45 per month instead of the December figure of $6.05.

Fuel and light for workers soared again in January. Coal briquettes rose from $3.95 per 100 chin during the previous month to nearly $4.30 in January. Charcoal was sold at $6.44 per basket as compared with the $6.25 for December.

The clothing group showed a rise of from 6 to 11 per cent, the high cost of dyestuffs and raw materials being the chief factors. The 68.42 per cent rise in the price of tea over December was the most conspicuous among the miscellaneous items.

"Cheap Sales"

To relieve the hardship of the poor, the Shanghai Committee for Cheap Sale of Rice was formed and sales started on January 21. Broken Saigon rice was sold at $1 for 6½ chin, or $24 per shih. The maximum purchase is limited to $1 per person.

A hot rice campaign was launched by the Salvation Army, distributing paper bags containing one pound of hot rice to starving beggars.
pages.zh:
工部局报告称
本地生活成本飙升至新高

根据上海公共租界工部局工业科昨日发布的报告，一月份上海的生活成本出现了前所未有的增长。

基于对本市工人的调查，该报告发现，虽然商品价格比1926年上涨了325%，但中国货币的购买力下降了略多于30分。

据报道，与上月相比，一月份的价格呈现全面上涨，平均涨幅从10%到超过100%不等。

在所有商品中，蔬菜的价格涨幅最大。青菜价格较12月的报价上涨了高达103%。菠菜上涨了81%，豆饼和萝卜上涨了超过45%。

肉类价格飙升

肉类、鱼类和禽类也出现显著上涨，涨幅从鲜猪肉的约7%到鲜鱼的26%不等。

豆油和猪油下跌了约10%，这与前一个月的大幅上涨形成例外。

尽管报告显示米价保持相当稳定，每石价格在37至39元之间，但面粉价格从每袋8.60美元上涨至超过10美元。

豆腐是工人广泛食用的食品，其一月份的成本远高于十二月，炸豆腐在十二月的报价为每块65分，而一月份则为每斤80分。

租金上涨

调查显示，一月份租金再次跳涨，较12月的指数上升了近10%。例如，工人每月需支付6.45美元，而12月的数字为6.05美元。

一月份工人的燃料和照明费用再次飙升。煤球从上月的每百斤3.95美元上涨至一月份的近4.30美元。木炭售价为每篮6.44美元，而12月为6.25美元。

服装类价格上涨了6%至11%，染料和原材料成本高企是主要因素。在杂项中，茶叶价格较12月上涨68.42%最为显眼。

“平价销售”

为缓解穷人的困境，上海平价米销售委员会成立，并于1月21日开始销售。碎西贡米以1元买6.5斤的价格出售，即每石24元。每人最高限购金额为1元。

救世军发起了一场热饭运动，向饥饿的乞丐分发装有一磅热米饭的纸袋。

pages.en:
Employees Of
SMC Given
Rice Money

Chinese employees of the
Shanghai Municipal Council
will receive a rice allowance—
in addition to the "high cost of
living allowance" of 30 per cent
of monthly pay granted recent-
ly—because of the abnormally
high price of rice, it was an-
nounced yesterday.

With effect from January this
year, a rice allowance will be issued
to those employees who receive
salaries of 100 dollars or less per
month whose names appear on the
departmental monthly pay sheets,
of half the difference between a
basic rice price of 12 dollars per
picul of 176 pounds and the average
daily price of rice for the period
from the 16th day of the preceding
month to the 15th day of the
month for which the allowance is
being computed, the announcement
read.

There will be a maximum
allowance in any one month of
seven dollars. Employees who
receive consideration from the
Council in respect to messing
are excluded from participation
in the allowance, the announce-
ment provided.

Various formulae for affording re-
lief were investigated and mem-
bers had before them data as to
relief granted in the case of sever-
al banks and commercial firms, it
was reported.
pages.zh:
工部局雇员
获发米贴

昨日宣布，由于米价异常高涨，上海公共租界工部局的中国雇员将获得米贴——这是在最近授予的相当于月薪30%的“高昂生活成本津贴”之外的额外补贴。

公告称，从今年一月起，凡月薪在100美元及以下、名字出现在部门月薪单上的雇员，将获得米贴。米贴金额为每石（176磅）12美元的基本米价与计算津贴所属月份的前一个月16日至当月15日期间每日平均米价之间差额的一半。

任何单月的最高津贴额为7美元。公告规定，享受工部局膳食待遇的雇员不得参与此项津贴。

据报道，会议调查了各种救济方案，委员们面前摆有关于几家银行和商业公司给予救济的数据。

pages.en:
Hotels To Raise Rates Due
To General Rise Of Prices

Confirmation of the report that
local hotels were raising their rates
due to the general increase in prices,
especially those of coal, was made
to THE CHINA PRESS yesterday by
the manager of a leading Shang-
hai hotel.
Rates in his hotel, he said,
would be increased on or about
March 1 by roughly 20 per cent.
He felt sure that other hotels -
would be forced to take the
same step, as "running a hotel
now, with everything rising in
cost from day to day, is an ex-
tremely difficult proposition."
Other hotel managers questioned
on the matter would not make a
definite statement on any proposed
increase in rates, but intimated
that as the prices they charged
their tenants dictated by the prices
they had to pay for food, coal and
other necessities, they could not say
today what they would have to do
tomorrow.
One hotel manager revealed
that he was raising the price of
ice in his hotel, as to continue
at the present prices would
mean to operate on a loss. The
same manager admitted that the
main factor which could force
Shanghai hotels to raise prices
was the "catastrophical" in-
crease in the cost of coal.
The cost of distilled water will
also be increased, it was an-
nounced yesterday by the Ac-
quarius Company. According to
this announcement, the com-
pany was compelled by the
"unprecedented increase in
the cost of raw materials" to
charge 25 cents extra for a 5
gallon jar of Distilled Water,
and 25 cents extra for a dozen
bottles of Aerated Water.
A step towards higher prices was
also taken yesterday by the
Roosevelt Terminal, which an-
nounced that as from March 1,
storage rates on cargoes at their
wharves would be subject to an ad-
ditional increase of 30 per cent.
The announcement further stated
that the free storage period would
be limited to 10 days, irrespective
of the port of origin.
pages.zh:
因物价普遍上涨
酒店将提高费率

上海一家主要酒店的经理昨日向《字林西报》证实了当地酒店因物价普遍上涨（尤其是煤炭价格）而提高费率的报道。
他说，他所在酒店的费率将在3月1日左右提高约20%。他确信其他酒店也将被迫采取同样的步骤，因为“在目前一切成本逐日上涨的情况下经营酒店是一项极其困难的事情。”
其他被问及此事的酒店经理不愿就拟议的费率增加发表明确声明，但暗示，由于他们向住客收取的价格取决于他们必须为食物、煤炭和其他必需品支付的价格，他们无法今天说明天会做什么。
一位酒店经理透露，他正在提高酒店内的冰块价格，因为维持现行价格意味着亏损经营。同一位经理承认，迫使上海酒店提高价格的主要因素是煤炭成本的“灾难性”增加。

阿克瓦里乌斯公司（Acquarius Company）昨日宣布，蒸馏水的成本也将增加。根据该公告，由于“原材料成本空前上涨”，该公司被迫对每5加仑装的蒸馏水额外收取25美分，对每打瓶装汽水额外收取25美分。

罗斯福码头（Roosevelt Terminal）昨日也采取了提价措施，宣布从3月1日起，其码头的货物仓储费率将额外增加30%。公告进一步指出，无论原产地港口为何，免费仓储期将限制为10天。

pages.en:
IL 2

Meat Monopoly Seen
99 Per Cent Pigs Imported
Here Land At Yangtszepoo

That Shanghai's cattle market, has been turned into a "Special Municipality" monopoly was shown in a Public Health Department report, issued yesterday, which stated that 99 per cent of the pigs imported during the month to Shanghai passed through the "Shanghai Livestock Market."

As compared with 86,951 pigs which came through the Yangtszepoo market, the number of pigs landed on the Settlement Bund totalled only 35 for the month. In December the number was 31, it was stated.

The same condition prevailed in the case of other livestock. It was reported that while 736 oxen, 248 buffaloes, 403 goats and 783 baskets of fowl landed on the Bund, live-stock landed at Yangtszepoo totalled 1,796 oxen, 2,626 buffaloes, 2,654 goats, 2,278 sheep and 5,325 fowl.

Abattoir Less Active
Reflecting the meat supply condition in the Settlement and Concession, the S.M.C. municipal abattoir showed further decrease in its activities during last month, stated the January report.

The report revealed that 9,165 animals were slaughtered in the abattoir, as compared with 10,176 for December.

Conditions at the meat market and cold storage also showed a drop in the quantity of goods handled, it was added, although a slight increase in the activities at the disposal plant was recorded.

Animals Examined
More than 600 animals from six dairies were given routine examinations by the Department while tubercular tests were given 198 animals. Of the latter number, it was found that 36 showed positive reactors. Ten animals were disposed on account of having been diseased.

A total of 353 routine inspections of meat export establishments were carried out in January as against 231 during the previous month.
pages.zh:
IL 2

肉类垄断显现
99%的进口猪只
在此于杨树浦登陆

昨日发布的一份公共卫生处报告显示，上海的牛市场已变成“特别市”的垄断市场，该报告指出，上月进口到上海的猪只有99%通过了“上海牲畜市场”。

与经由杨树浦市场进入的86,951头猪相比，上月在租界外滩登陆的猪只总数仅为35头。据称，12月份这一数字为31头。

其他牲畜的情况也是如此。据报道，虽然在外滩登陆的有736头牛、248头水牛、403只山羊和783篮家禽，但在杨树浦登陆的牲畜总数为1,796头牛、2,626头水牛、2,654只山羊、2,278只绵羊和5,325只家禽。

屠宰场活动减少

一月报告称，反映出租界和法租界的肉类供应状况，工部局市政屠宰场上月的活动进一步减少。

报告显示，屠宰场屠宰了9,165头动物，而12月份为10,176头。

报告还补充说，肉类市场和冷库处理的货物数量也出现下降，尽管处置厂的活动略有增加。

动物检查

卫生处对来自六家奶牛场的600多头动物进行了例行检查，并对198头动物进行了结核病测试。在后一组中，发现有36头呈阳性反应。十头动物因患病而被处置。

一月份共对肉类出口机构进行了353次例行检查，而上个月为231次。

pages.en:
Forged Meat Stamps :
A Reader's Vigilance

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—The mere fact that "the ques-
tion of fraudulent stamping of but-
chery meat has not escaped the at-
tention of the F.C. authorities" as re-
plied by MONSIEUR J. BARDIAN on
February 17 is ample proof that my
statement to this effect was not
sheer imagination.
As to his accusation that I failed
to report this matter to the Public
Health Department, may I assure
him that when I wanted to do so
that particular part of meat bearing
the stamp was sold already. How-
ever, I am closely watching my
neighbouring butcher and should an-
other occasion present itself, believe
me I will not spare him. Should
however ALLEN EOO's friend like to
become "interested," I enclose here-
with the address of the shop in
question and if he cares to relieve
me of my task, and keep himself a
watchful eye on it, he will soon find
out that my contention was not
baseless.
As for ALLEN EOO's doubting the
fact of horse meat being sold in the
F.C.—since it was duly stamped, why
not? And, of course, in this case
there could be no question of a falsi-
fied stamp. Further, the fact that
some people may buy horse meat,
does not necessarily prove their
stupidity, I would rather call it
ignorance or just a matter of taste.
Are there not people who have a
liking for cockroaches or frogs, so
why not horse meat? Actually now,
buffalo meat is very much in vogue,
but I would not call the purchasing
of it an "extreme foolishness" either,
since 1st quality meat is practically
unobtainable in the smaller butcheries
and not many can afford to patronize
the compradore shops and pay
double prices or take up the sport
of going every morning to the
market where one can have a choice.
QUO VADIS.
Shanghai, Feb. 21.
pages.zh:
伪造肉类印章：
一位读者的警惕

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生——正如J. BARDIAN先生于2月17日所回复的那样，“法租界当局并未忽视屠宰肉类欺诈性盖章的问题”，这一事实本身就充分证明，我对此事的陈述并非凭空想象。

至于他指责我未向公共卫生处报告此事，我可以向他保证，当我打算这样做时，那块带有印章的特定部分的肉已经售出。然而，我正密切监视着我隔壁的肉贩，如果再有类似情况发生，请相信我不会放过他。不过，如果ALLEN EOO的朋友愿意“感兴趣”，我随信附上涉事店铺的地址，如果他愿意替我分担这项任务，并亲自对其保持警惕，他很快就会发现我的主张并非毫无根据。

至于ALLEN EOO怀疑在法租界出售马肉的事实——既然它盖有正式印章，为何不可？当然，在这种情况下，不存在伪造印章的问题。此外，有些人可能购买马肉，这并不一定证明他们愚蠢，我宁愿称之为无知或仅仅是口味问题。难道没有人喜欢吃蟑螂或青蛙吗，那么为什么不能吃马肉呢？实际上，现在水牛肉非常流行，但我也不会称购买水牛肉是“极度的愚蠢”，因为在小肉铺里几乎买不到一级肉，而没多少人能负担得起光顾买办商店并支付双倍价格，或者采取每天早上去市场挑选的这种“消遣”。

QUO VADIS.
上海，2月21日。

CHINA PRESS

FEB 23 1940

Rice Market

rate of white rice declined yesterday, best
quality of white rice being quoted at

business transacted in the session was
estimated at 3,000 bags.

《大美晚报》

1940年2月23日

米市

FEB 1 7 1940

Hungry Mobs Loot
Two Rice Shops
In Northern Areas

Indication that Shanghai may
soon witness more rice riots in
the near future as a result of
prevailing high prices was seen
yesterday when two rice shops
north of Soochow Creek were
raided by small mobs of hungry
Chinese.

The raids occurred about 1.30
p.m.. One was staged at a rice
shop at 779 Tengshan Road
while the other was carried out
at 675 East Yuhang Road. In
both cases, the police arrived and
dispersed the rioters. Only small
amounts of rice were stolen.

FEB 1 7 1940

High Prices:
And Other Rackets

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—I presume OLD BABOOSHKA is
probably on a vegetable and milk
diet on account of her age and there-
fore is not so well informed of the
meat situation.
As a matter of fact, not only did
meat prices not decline, but they
have still advanced after the holi-
days, so a pound of beef steak which
cost on the eve of the Chinese New
Year $0.80 is now $1.10 per lb.
Moreover, there is noticeable scarcity
of fresh meat in the butcheries,
which fact seems to me a clever
manoeuvre to further boost up the
price of this commodity.
Besides coal, I cannot name any
other imported article which has
multiplied so many times its pre-
war price as this local stuff.
By the way, some readers may be
interested to hear about my ex-
perience. Yesterday, early in the
morning, when I went to my neigh-
bouring shops to buy something for
breakfast, I noticed an employee
busily engaged in drawing a circle
with a blue pencil on a piece of
meat which afterwards took a
resemblance to the F.M.C. stamp.
Again, some time ago I witnessed in
another shop an employee selling
horse meat with the stamp "Cheval"
for veal cutlets and charging it
accordingly.
In conclusion I should say that if
some officials would like to take a
stroll one of these mornings and visit
some Chinese groceries they would
be shocked to see (or is it a revela-
tion to them?) any kind of inscrip-
tions on the various meats displayed
there, but very seldom would they
find the genuine F.M.C. 1st quality
blue stamp on it.
QUO VADIS.
Shanghai, Feb. 15.
pages.zh:
1940年2月17日

高价：
及其他骗局

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生——我推测OLD BABOOSHKA可能因为年龄关系，饮食以蔬菜和牛奶为主，因此对肉类行情不太了解。

事实上，肉类价格不仅没有下降，而且在节后继续上涨，所以春节前夜 costing（花费）0.80美元一磅的牛排，现在是每磅1.10美元。此外，肉铺里的鲜肉明显短缺，在我看来，这似乎是一种进一步推高该商品价格的巧妙手段。

除了煤炭，我说不出还有哪种进口商品像这种本地货一样，价格比战前翻了许多倍。

顺便说一下，有些读者可能有兴趣听听我的经历。昨天清晨，当我去附近的商店买早餐用品时，我注意到一名店员正忙着用蓝铅笔在一块肉上画圈，这块肉后来看起来很像法租界公董局（F.M.C.）的印章。另外，不久前我在另一家商店目睹一名店员将盖有“Cheval”（法语：马）印章的马肉当作小牛肉排出售，并按此收费。

最后我想说，如果某些官员愿意在这些天的早晨散步并参观一些中国杂货店，他们会震惊地看到（或者这对他们来说是个启示？）陈列的各种肉类上有任何种类的标记，但很少会在上面找到真正的法租界公董局一级蓝色印章。

QUO VADIS.
上海，2月15日。

pages.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

FEB 1 7 1940

Appeal To City Fathers
To the Editor of the
"NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS"
Sir,—I believe that I shall be voicing the opinion of the public, if I were to say that we are practically all fed up with the food racketeers and profiteers of this town. There is no real reason why the price of local fresh products should have risen to such an extent. It is about time that the City Fathers of both Concessions should form a Food Committee to curb the rapacities of the butchers and grocers.
It is really disgraceful for a City like ours, boasting of such intelligent executives in the Council Office, to have overlooked this matter. I daresay Miss Hinder would have been better employed if she had been deputed to look into this affair.
There is only one way in dealing with these profiteers, either, by a heavy fine or imprisonment or cancellation of trade licence.
It is up to the authorities concerned to take drastic action immediately, otherwise, these profiteers will soon come to believe that they are also "Al. Capones" and will continue to increase prices of food stuff with impunity.
Fed Up
Shanghai, Feb. 16.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，

1940年2月17日

呼吁市政当局

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生——如果我说我们实际上都受够了这座城市的食品投机商和牟取暴利者，我相信我是在表达公众的意见。本地新鲜产品价格上升到如此程度，并没有真正的理由。两个租界的“城市父老”（市政当局）是时候成立一个食品委员会，以遏制屠夫和杂货商的贪婪了。

对于我们这样一座以市政厅拥有如此睿智的行政人员而自豪的城市来说，忽视这个问题真是可耻。我敢说，如果指派Hinder小姐调查此事，她会更有用武之地。

对付这些牟取暴利者只有一种方法，要么处以重罚或监禁，要么吊销贸易执照。

有关当局必须立即采取严厉行动，否则，这些牟取暴利者很快就会认为他们也是“阿尔·卡彭”（Al. Capones），并将继续肆无忌惮地提高食品价格。

受够了
上海，2月16日。

pages.en:
NO. DAILY N
JUL 17 1940

High Living Costs
Readers have aired very exhaustively their views regarding the unprecedented increase in the cost of living within the last month and, particularly since the China New Year. A variety of reasons has been offered to explain the extreme upward tendency in prices. These have ranged from the quotation of the economic rule of supply and demand at a time of the year, when spending by China's millions is greater than at other periods, to bald accusations of profiteering by dealers controlling the foodstuffs and commodities of the population of Shanghai. Exchange, of course, has a lot to do with this extraordinary situation but there still remains to be found a logical explanation. Take, for instance, the price of coal which is somewhere about $200 a ton and is likely to go higher. Japan has been a large purchaser throughout the Far East owing to the drought and consequent reduction of hydro-electric power resources, and freights are unusually high in consequence of this factor and the European war but even at $200, or approximately £4 a ton, with the possibility of increasing to the equivalent of £6 a ton, coal prices compare unfavourably with Europe where war necessities have transformed market conditions but nothing similar to the extent reflected by such a price in Shanghai. A comparison of local market prices in February last year and February this year would make one believe that all sense of proportion has vanished in this part of the world. Last February coal was $50 a ton, rice $15 a picul and meat was well below a dollar per pound. The householder needs no reminding of the present scale of prices which show daily increases and will refuse to subscribe to the argument that the higher cost of production warrants the disproportionate increase in prices. Some of the most ordinary kitchen items show amazing changes. One simple example suffices. Bamboo shoots, from China's traditional tree, sold at 25 cents a pound last February and are now nearly a dollar a pound. Nobody would say that foreign exchange or any of the other glib assertions should cause this. A similar condition involves all locally-produced foodstuffs which certainly should not be so greatly affected by the factors applying to imports based on foreign exchange. The volume of public protest has not yet induced any official action to control prices but circumstances strongly emphasize the urgency.
pages.zh:
编号：每日新闻
1940年7月17日

生活成本高昂

读者们已极为详尽地发表了他们关于过去一个月内、特别是自中国新年以来生活成本空前上涨的看法。人们提出了各种理由来解释价格的极端上涨趋势。这些理由 ranging from 引用一年中某些时期（此时中国数百万人的支出高于其他时期）的供需经济法则，到赤裸裸地指责控制上海居民食品和商品交易的商人牟取暴利。当然，汇率与这种异常局势有很大关系，但仍需找到一个合乎逻辑的解释。以煤炭价格为例，目前约为每吨200美元，且可能进一步上涨。由于干旱以及随之而来的水力发电资源减少，日本在整个远东地区一直是大量购买者，而受此因素及欧洲战争的影响，运费异常高昂。但即便按每吨200美元（约合4英镑）计算，且有可能增至相当于每吨6英镑的水平，上海的煤价与欧洲相比仍处于不利地位；在欧洲，战争需求虽已改变了市场状况，但其价格涨幅并未达到上海所反映的程度。将去年二月与今年二月的本地市场价格进行比较，会让人觉得这个世界的一部分已失去了所有的比例感。去年二月，煤炭为每吨50美元，大米为每担15美元，肉类价格远低于每磅1美元。家庭主妇无需提醒即可感知当前的价格水平，这些价格日日上涨，她们拒绝接受“生产成本上升证明价格不成比例上涨是合理的”这一论点。一些最普通的厨房用品价格出现了惊人的变化。举一个简单的例子就足够了。作为中国传统树木产物的竹笋，去年二月售价为每磅25美分，而现在接近每磅1美元。没有人会说这是由外汇或任何其他花言巧语般的断言所导致的。类似的情况涉及所有本地生产的食品，这些因素显然不应像基于外汇的进口商品那样受到如此大的影响。公众抗议的声浪尚未促使当局采取任何行动来控制价格，但局势强烈强调了此举的紧迫性。

pages.en:
FEB 16 1940
High Prices Stir
Chinese
Authorities Urged to Check
Upward Tendency; Rice and
Coal Show Big Increases

The rapid increase in commodity prices in Shanghai during the past few days has created an alarming situation which is the chief topic of household discussions throughout the city. Hope is expressed by the Chinese press and residents that the authorities concerned should do something to relieve the situation before it is too late as the price of even Saigon rice now has surpassed the $50 mark as compared with the former price of $35 or little more when rice riots broke out in the city. The price of native rice is fastly approaching the $60 mark.

As was recently predicted, the price of native rice per picul has increased beyond the $50 mark after the Lunar New Year, the officially fixed price of $40, which is already too high for the average resident, never having been followed by merchants during the past few days. The upward trend was followed just prior to the Lunar New Year but it was then thought to be the usual condition during such a period when buying activities were accelerated, but since the Lunar New Year day the increase of prices has taken most residents unawares since violent increases were registered overnight.

It is learned, however, that the new rice situation is more difficult to control than the situation existing some weeks ago when hoarding and control effected outside the foreign areas were mentioned as chief reasons for the trouble. This time, it is said, the increase is registered chiefly owing to the unfavourable rate of exchange which must be used for buying Saigon rice. The increase was therefore first seen in the local Saigon rice market where formerly most rice-eating people looked for relief as its price was cheaper. Prices of yellow beans, bean oil and flour have all been increased to unprecedented levels.

Coal at $120 Tons

Just as the price of rice has become five times bigger so is the price of coal breaking the $200 mark per ton. The action of some coal merchants is criticized since in addition to hoarding with which they are charged by the Chinese press, they also delay sending goods to customers when ordered. This was most evident yesterday when numerous Chinese housewives complained that they did not receive coal balls (needed for cooking by practically every Chinese family) ordered the previous day. The cargo was there but the delay in sending would mean an additional dollar's profit. The price of a picul of coal balls on Wednesday was $5.80 as compared with about $1 during pre-war days. The price jumped to over $6 yesterday.

The problem is very complicated and no official efforts have so far been made to prevent a general increase of prices although it has been suggested that a price-fixing committee be created. A secretary of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce said yesterday that his Chamber could not do anything at the moment and that the same body had not petitioned the Shanghai Municipal Council to act on the subject. The "Central China Daily News" attributed the unprecedented increase of prices to the "unstable financial situation" resulting from the decrease of the Chinese dollar and suggested that cessation of hostilities would bring relief.
pages.zh:
1940年2月16日
高价引发中国人关注
敦促当局遏制上涨趋势；大米和煤炭价格大幅上涨

过去几天上海商品价格的快速上涨造成了一种令人警觉的局势，这已成为全市家庭讨论的主要话题。中国媒体和居民表示希望有关当局在事态恶化之前采取行动缓解局势，因为甚至西贡米的价格现在已超过50美元大关，而此前该市发生米骚乱时价格仅为35美元或略多。国产大米价格正迅速逼近60美元大关。

正如近期预测的那样，农历新年后国产大米每担价格已突破50美元大关，商户在过去几天从未遵守官方固定的40美元价格，该价格对普通居民而言已经过高。上涨趋势在农历新年前夕就已显现，但当时人们认为这是此类采购活动加速时期的常态；然而，自农历新年当天以来，价格的上涨让大多数居民措手不及，因为夜间出现了剧烈涨幅。

然而据了解，新的米市局势比几周前的情况更难控制，当时囤积居奇以及租界外实施的管控被认为是造成麻烦的主要原因。据说，此次价格上涨主要是由于购买西贡米必须使用的不利汇率所致。因此，涨价首先出现在本地西贡米市场，以前大多数以米为主食的人曾指望通过该市场获得缓解，因为其价格较为便宜。黄豆、豆油和面粉的价格也都涨到了前所未有的水平。

煤炭每吨120美元

正如大米价格涨了五倍一样，煤炭价格也突破了每吨200美元的大关。一些煤炭商人的行为受到批评，因为除了被中国媒体指控的囤积居奇外，他们在接到订单后还延迟向客户发货。这一点在昨天尤为明显，众多中国家庭主妇抱怨未收到前一天订购的煤球（几乎每个中国家庭做饭都需要）。货物就在仓库里，但延迟发货意味着额外的一美元利润。周三每担煤球的价格为5.80美元，而战前约为1美元。昨天价格跳涨至超过6美元。

问题非常复杂，尽管有人建议成立一个物价核定委员会，但迄今为止官方尚未做出任何努力来防止价格普遍上涨。一位中国总商会秘书昨天表示，他的商会目前无能为力，且该机构并未就此事项向上海公共租界工部局请愿。《华中日报》将这次空前的价格上涨归因于中国法币贬值导致的“金融局势不稳”，并建议停止敌对行动将带来缓解。

pages.en:
RISING COMMODITY
PRICES ALARMING

Chinese Agitating For
Official Control Of
Many Products

The abnormal high price of all
essential commodities, especially
that of coal, rice, and wheat flour.
is now causing the most serious
concern to Shanghai's public organi-
zations. Unless an effective rein
can be placed on the runaway
market, public safety in Shanghai
is bound to be affected.

Several organizations are looking
for official restraint through the
efforts of the S.M.C. and F.M.C.
Among these organizations is the
Citizens' Federation of the First
Special District, which is reported
to have sent a communication to
the two municipal authorities, re-
questing the introduction of some
effective measures to check pro-
fiteering

For the control of the rice mar-
ket, two powerful organizations are
already in existence, the Shanghai
Staple Food Regulation Committee
and the Shanghai Frumentation
Committee. How far these two com-
mittees will succeed in bringing
down or stabilizing the rice mar-
ket will depend entirely upon the
extent of support, financial and
otherwise, the public will accord
them. It is advocated that if many
public bodies or firms buy rice from
the non-profit rice committee in-
stead of from the rice merchants,
price advances would not be effect-
ed so rapidly.

It is also generally hoped that
some additional organizations will
be formed in the shortest time, to
attempt the control of coal and the
flour market, in the same manner
as the rice committee, are now
doing their work.

As one of the worst victims of
the high coal price, the local bath-
house trade is understood to have
petitioned the S.M.C. to place a
curb on further increases.
pages.zh:
商品价格上涨
令人担忧

中国人呼吁官方
管控多种产品

所有必需品的异常高价，特别是煤炭、大米和小麦面粉的价格，现在正引起上海公共团体的最严重关切。除非能对失控的市场进行有效约束，否则上海的公共安全必将受到影响。

几个组织正通过上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）和法租界公董局（F.M.C.）的努力寻求官方约束。其中包括第一特区市民联合会，据报道该会已向两个市政当局致函，请求引入一些有效措施以遏制牟取暴利行为。

为了控制大米市场，已经存在两个强有力的组织，即上海主食调节委员会和上海粮食委员会。这两个委员会在降低或稳定大米市场方面能取得多大成功，完全取决于公众给予它们的财政及其他支持的程度。有人主张，如果许多公共团体或公司从无利润大米委员会而不是从米商处购买大米，价格上涨就不会如此迅速。

人们还普遍希望尽快成立一些额外的组织，以像大米委员会目前所做的那样，尝试控制煤炭和面粉市场。

作为高煤价的最严重受害者之一，据悉本地浴室行业已向上海公共租界工部局请愿，要求遏制进一步的涨价。

pages.en:
Price Increase Must Be Checked

WHATEVER may be the backing and the past record of the First District Citizens' Federation, the petition it sent to the Shanghai Municipal Council for checking the activities of the local profiteers should receive the serious consideration of the Settlement governing body.

The increase in the costs of living in Shanghai, which has registered a further rise since the Chinese New Year holidays, has long passed the stage wherein it could be treated with official and civic complacence. It is plain that something must be done, and done immediately, in order to enable hundreds of thousands of low-bracket wage earners to live, to eat and to survive.

According to investigations made by this newspaper, rice prices have reached the unprecedented peak of $54 a picul. Dealers are of the opinion that unless some measure is taken, Saigon rice will soon skyrocket to $80 a picul. The present increase and the anticipated further rise are partly due to the mounting freight charges. But this evidently is not the only reason. Profiteering in rice has sent the prices up and will continue to send the prices up unless more drastic steps are taken by the Shanghai Municipal Council and the French Municipal Council.

* * *

IN the middle of December last year, the Shanghai Municipal Council and the French Municipal Council issued a joint proclamation in which they threatened to expel from the areas within their jurisdiction people who manipulate the prices of rice. This measure was taken on the ground that profiteering in rice, the staple food of the Chinese populace, menaces the public safety and welfare of Shanghai.

At the time that the proclamation was made public, this newspaper stated that the step was a laudable official gesture, but its ultimate usefulness would depend upon the rigid enforcement of the order promulgated by the Concession and the Settlement governing body. The fact that the price of rice has registered another sharp increase and that it is slated for a further rise would indicate that there is a need on the part of the two Councils to take further substantial measures to put teeth into their December proclamation.

* * *

THE increase in the price of rice is not the only disturbing factor in the local commodity situation. The price of soft coal, according to a report appearing in this newspaper, is likely to reach $350 a ton. At the same time, other daily necessities such as vegetables, meat, oil, and clothing have all shown a tendency of further increases.

Evidently the price situation today cannot be checked by piecemeal adjustment. If any result is to be achieved at all, it can be achieved only by giving consideration to the question of commodity prices in its entirety. In other words, the administrative organizations having jurisdiction in Shanghai must take steps to check not only the price of rice, but also to devise suitable measures to brake the increases of other commodity prices such as that of coal, vegetables and other daily necessities.

Furthermore, in dealing with the question of commodity prices, the two Councils must also abandon their former view that the problem is essentially of an emergency and temporary nature, and that consequently the remedial measures devised need only be of a stop-gap variety. The situation today shows that the question of high living costs and high commodity prices has come for an extended stay in Shanghai, and to solve the problem the two Councils must take a longer range view of the issue.

* * *

IN this connection, it may also be necessary for the two Councils to devise proper ways to overcome the handicap of their limited legal authority. If the power which the Shanghai Municipal Council possesses by virtue of the Land Regulations is not sufficient to cope with the present crisis, then proper steps must be taken until this legal obstruction is removed. The commodity price question affects the welfare of so many millions of people and it is of so serious a nature that legal obstruction must not be allowed to remain as an excuse or reason for official inaction.

This newspaper is reasonably optimistic that if a required amount of enthusiasm and determination exists among the officials of the local governing organization, something can be done to check, at least partially, the rise in commodity prices. There are a number of possible channels which can be explored in this search for a way to remedy the present situation. A special committee, with substantial authority and civic support, may be organized to investigate the commodity price question in detail. If as a result of this investigation, it is shown that a serious shortage exists in rice, coal and other goods, some ways can be devised for the Councils to import the needed commodities in order to relieve the shortage. These and other measures may come under the general heading of "welfare enterprises."

On the other hand, and coming under the general heading of "law enforcement," the Councils may take additional steps to check profiteering. The proclamation which was made with regard to rice profiteering should be extended to include profiteering in other essential goods and services.

The suggestion we have made may indeed sound ambitious and difficult. But the present situation is growing so serious that morally and legally, the Councils cannot dismiss the whole thing with the blanket phrase, "it cannot be done." It is up to the two Councils to try, and try until they succeed.
pages.zh:
必须遏制物价上涨

无论第一区市民联合会拥有何种背景及过往记录，其向上海公共租界工部局提交的、请求遏制本地奸商活动的请愿书，应当得到租界管理机构的认真考虑。

上海的生活成本自农历新年假期以来进一步上升，早已超过了官方和市民可以安之若素、掉以轻心的阶段。显然，必须立即采取行动，以使数十万低收入阶层的工资收入者能够维持生活、糊口并生存下去。

据本报调查，米价已达到每担54元的前所未有的峰值。经销商认为，除非采取某些措施，否则西贡米的价格很快将飙升至每担80元。目前的上涨以及预期的进一步攀升，部分原因是由于运费不断上涨。但这显然不是唯一的原因。大米投机行为推高了价格，并且除非上海公共租界工部局和法公董局采取更严厉的措施，否则价格将继续上涨。

* * *

去年12月中旬，上海公共租界工部局和法公董局发布联合公告，威胁将操纵米价的人驱逐出其管辖区域。采取这一措施的理由是，作为中国民众主食的大米的投机行为，危及上海的公共安全与福利。

在该公告公布时，本报曾指出，这一步骤是值得称赞的官方姿态，但其最终效用取决于租界和定居点管理机构对所颁布命令的严格执行。事实上，米价再次大幅上涨，且预计还将进一步上升，这表明两个理事会需要采取进一步的实质性措施，为其12月的公告赋予真正的执行力。

* * *

米价上涨并非本地商品局势中唯一的令人不安的因素。据本报刊登的一篇报道，软煤价格可能达到每吨350元。与此同时，蔬菜、肉类、油和衣物等其他日常必需品也均显示出进一步上涨的趋势。

显然，今天的物价形势不能靠零敲碎打的调整来遏制。如果要取得任何成效，只能从整体上考量商品价格问题。换言之，在上海拥有管辖权的行政组织必须采取措施，不仅遏制米价，还要制定适当的措施以抑制煤炭、蔬菜和其他日常必需品等其他商品价格的上涨。

此外，在处理商品价格问题时，两个理事会还必须放弃以往的观点，即认为该问题本质上是紧急和暂时性的，因此所设计的补救措施只需是权宜之计。目前的局势表明，高生活成本和高商品价格问题将在上海长期存在，为解决这一问题，两个理事会必须对该问题采取更长远的视角。

* * *

在这方面，两个理事会可能还需要设计适当的方法，以克服其法律权限有限的障碍。如果上海公共租界工部局凭借《土地章程》所拥有的权力不足以应对当前的危机，那么必须采取适当步骤，直到消除这一法律障碍为止。商品价格问题关系到数百万人的福利，性质如此严重，决不允许将法律障碍作为官方不作为的借口或理由。

本报持谨慎乐观态度，认为如果地方管理机构的官员具备必要的热情和决心，至少可以在部分程度上遏制商品价格的上涨。在寻求 remedy 当前局势的途径方面，有许多可能的渠道可供探索。可以组建一个拥有实质权力和市民支持特别委员会，详细调查商品价格问题。如果调查结果显示大米、煤炭和其他货物存在严重短缺，则可以设计一些方法，由理事会进口所需商品以缓解短缺。这些及其他措施可归入“福利事业”的大类之下。

另一方面，归入“执法”大类之下，理事会可以采取额外步骤来遏制投机倒把。针对大米投机的公告应扩展至包括其他基本商品和服务的投机行为。

我们提出的建议听起来确实雄心勃勃且困难重重。但目前的局势日益严峻，在道德和法律上，理事会都不能用“此事办不到”这一笼统的说法将整个事件置之不理。两个理事会有责任进行尝试，并坚持尝试直至成功。

pages.en:
FEB 1 6 1940

BEAN CURD PRICES
ARE INCREASED

Abnormal Increase In
Local Market Rates
Cause Hardship

Joining the general advance of
all essential commodities, the price
of soy beans has also shot up con-
siderably after the Spring Holidays.
It was quoted yesterday from some
$26.50 a picul for Wuhu beans to
over $29 for Tsingtao products.
Dairen beans were sold about the
same price as those from Wuhu.
This represented a jump of $6 a
picul over the closing prices of the
Chinese year-end. Wuhu beans were
then selling under $21, already con-
sidered as a peak price.
Immediate effect of the raise in
bean prices is the increase in the
price of bean curds, a daily food for
all classes of Chinese people, effec-
tive immediately, the bean curd
stores are selling at their new prices.
A single piece of "hard" curd, cost-
ing only a few coppers before the
war, now sells for 10 cents. A piece
of white "soft" curd, which used
to cost two or three coppers, is now
three cents. A slab of the latter
now costs $1.30. All other by-pro-
ducts of bean curd, such as the
bean-milk skim, has been advanced
in price proportionately.
This is the second price increase
of bean curds, the previous instance
was effective last December.
In view of the acuteness of the
rice situation, the Shanghai Bean
and Rice Guild, which governs the
local Rice Market on Foochow Road,
will convene an urgent meeting this
afternoon at 4 o'clock to discuss
various measures. The Guild has
already sent representatives to call
on Mr. T. K. Ho, Deputy Secretary
of S.M.C., to report on the rice
situation.
pages.zh:
1940年2月16日

豆腐价格上涨

本地市场汇率异常上涨
造成困境

随着所有基本必需品的普遍涨价，春节过后大豆价格也大幅飙升。昨日报价显示，芜湖豆从每担约26.50元涨至青岛产品超过29元。大连豆的售价与芜湖豆大致相同。这代表比中国年底收盘价每担上涨了6元。当时芜湖豆售价低于21元，已被视为峰值价格。

豆价上涨的直接后果是豆腐价格的上涨，豆腐是所有阶层中国人的日常食物，即日起，豆腐店已开始按新价格出售。一块“硬”豆腐，战前仅需几个铜板，现在售价为1角。一块白色的“软”豆腐，过去需两三个铜板，现在为3分。一方后者现在 costing 1.30元。所有其他豆腐副产品，如豆浆皮，价格也按比例上涨。

这是豆腐的第二次涨价，上一次生效是在去年12月。

鉴于米况严峻，管理福州路本地米市的上海豆米业公会将于今天下午4时召开紧急会议，讨论各项措施。该公会已派代表拜访上海公共租界工部局副秘书 T. K. Ho（何德奎，音译）先生，汇报米市情况。

pages.en:
High Prices :
New Year Spending

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Having seen SOUP MEAT's letter on the rather unreasonable hike of prices during the few days preceding the China New Year, I am not surprised at all, as it is the age-old custom in this city (or country) to indulge in this "sort of privilege" as SOUP MEAT will soon find out if he stays longer in China.

There can be one or two explanations but they are all largely psychological, being influenced by the exuberance of spending at this time of year. Usually before the Spring Festivals every Chinese has or manages to get an abundance of cash to prepare for its celebration. Then there is the custom of paying out bonuses before the China New Year. One way or the other shopkeepers know that the public have plenty of free cash with which to make last-minute purchases to lay in for those days during New Year when there would be a hiatus in trading. So the situation resolves itself into this: The Public are keen to buy; they have plenty of money; the shops are to be closed for the holidays; and so why not make a clean breast of it?

Taking advantage of the situation, middle-class barbers in town also charge double prices and the tips in Chinese restaurants follow threefold, fourfold or as the avarice of the restaurant-keepers may dictate. Rickshaw pullers are not to be outdone and usually ask for some extra 'consolations'; house-servants receive "red-packets"; and it would appear that the most miserly among the city's population could also afford to be more lavish in their personal appearance on this day of days.

This year particularly the hike in prices seems to assume dumbfounded proportions as the "go-getting" among traders grows from bad to worse knowing that no effective regulations exist for the control of prices in this "great" city. Who suffers then? The small wage-earner, the office worker, the labourer. The economic scale is turned against these unfortunate individuals who sweat from day to day only to indulge in a little peak-spending at this time of year. The logical conclusion is that if they had no previous savings they either borrowed or begged, and the further consequence of this is obvious from the crime reports in the papers.

Ours is a most wonderful city. It has charitable institutions galore, Salvation Army Hot-Rice Vans doing their nocturnal rounds, an almost continuous call for subscriptions for charitable purposes, which seems to speak a lot for the city's poor. Yet through it all, aside from this plausible gesture, there still remains much of the human greed for gains as evidenced by immoral exchange speculations, hoarding and manipulation of prices, shortweight scales, etc. A whole population of paupers has grown out of the aftermath of the Shanghai War and what these destitutes need is not so much ceaseless charity but a chance to regain their respect in the community; unfortunately, however, that can hardly be brought about so long as they continue to be mercilessly exploited by mercenary traders and employers alike.
K. H. B.
Shanghai, Feb. 14.
pages.zh:
高价：
新年开支

致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——看到 SOUP MEAT（音译）关于中国新年前几天物价不合理上涨的来信，我一点也不感到惊讶，因为在这座城市（或这个国家）， indulge in 这种“特权”是由来已久的习俗，如果 SOUP MEAT 在中国待得更久些，他很快就会发现这一点。

对此可以有一两种解释，但它们主要都是心理层面的，受此时节挥霍消费情绪的影响。通常在春节前，每个中国人都有或设法弄到大量现金来准备庆祝。此外，还有在春节前发放奖金的习俗。无论如何，店主们都知道公众手中有大量闲钱，用于在最后时刻购物，以备新年期间交易停滞的那几天之需。因此，局势演变为这样：公众热衷于购买；他们有钱；商店要关门过节；那么何不干脆大赚一笔呢？

利用这一局势，市内的中产阶级理发师也将价格加倍，中餐馆的小费则增至三倍、四倍，或由餐馆老板的贪婪程度决定。人力车夫也不甘落后，通常要求额外的“赏钱”；家仆收到“红包”；似乎连这座城市中最吝啬的居民，在这个特殊的日子里也能负担得起在个人外表上更加阔绰。

今年，物价上涨的幅度尤其令人瞠目结舌，因为商人中的“逐利”风气每况愈下，他们知道在这座“伟大”的城市中不存在有效的价格管制法规。那么谁受苦呢？是小工资收入者、职员、劳工。经济天平对这些不幸的人不利，他们日复一日地辛勤劳作，却只为了在这一年中的这个时候 indulging in 一点峰值消费。合乎逻辑的结论是，如果他们以前没有储蓄，他们要么借债，要么乞讨，而由此产生的进一步后果从报纸上的犯罪报告中显而易见。

我们的城市是一座非常奇妙的城市。这里有大量的慈善机构，救世军的施粥车夜间巡逻，几乎不间断地呼吁为慈善目的捐款，这似乎很大程度上是为了城市的穷人。然而，透过这一切，除了这种看似合理的姿态外，仍然存在着大量的人类贪欲，这体现在不道德的外汇投机、囤积居奇和操纵价格、短斤少两等行为上。上海战争的后果造就了一整群贫民，这些赤贫者需要的与其说是无休止的慈善，不如说是重新获得社区尊重的机会；然而不幸的是，只要他们继续被唯利是图的商人和雇主无情剥削，这种情况就很难实现。
K. H. B.
上海，2月14日

pages.en:
H. C. L. Enquiry :
Present Methods Criticized
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—My point in addressing you today, and in particular Miss Hinder, is solely for the purposes stated herein below. For various reasons, I would appreciate that Miss Hinder and her staff respect my identity which could be traced through her files.
I understand that Miss Hinder is not receiving the support from the community in her effort to arrive at, and to produce statistics showing the H.C.L. for foreigners, which the Council had put into her capable hands after having received many requests from various firms asking if they had any figures showing the H.C.L. for foreigners.
It is a pity that Miss Hinder is not receiving this support from the Shanghai Community, as we (if I may so say) the working class of the foreign community, have everything to gain by the establishment of the actual H.C.L. for foreigners.
Then why, why this lack of support? Obviously something is wrong or perhaps I should say, the inconvenience and trouble encountered by the housewives in conforming with the present system of keeping records as requested by Miss Hinder, not to mention frayed nerves and irritability met by home-coming husbands. For example, my wife did not complete her records the very first month, which ended when she very generously offered me the pleasure of doing them myself. She had no end of trouble with the cook and she was not going to lose him for another just as bad if not worse.
Most families living on budget, give their cooks a fixed amount for marketing daily, and cooks, as we all know, resent being questioned. They must make their usual squeeze and if you change your cook, it would be the same story all over again. So, if you are satisfied with the quality and quantity he puts on your table, you would sooner give up keeping these records rather than have him walk out on you.

Why ask several hundred housewives to write down the same things? They all pay for instance $5.50 per lb. for a certain brand of butter last week and $5.60 this week: so much for beef yesterday and so much today, etc., etc. Such details could be obtained from your own paper which publishes daily the current market prices, and Miss Hinder could too, obtain from several leading and otherwise storekeepers their current prices for groceries.
In my opinion, Miss Hinder is "barking up the wrong tree." Let us suppose a family man is earning a salary of say $400 per month and has not had an increase for several years nor is he receiving any H.C.L. allowance. His cost of living has not increased. He was able to live in a nice house or apartment, could afford to buy butter, eggs, milk and good beef, etc. Now, since one must live within one's own income, i.e. $400 he and his family are compelled to live in a one-room flat, eating margarine in lieu of butter, no eggs, no milk for the children, poor quality beef, and his wife keeps a record for Miss Hinder showing that margarine has gone up 20 cents in one week. Does that tell Miss Hinder his H.C.L.? It does not, because it has not gone up. What has really happened is that his standard of living has gone down tremendously and for him to maintain his old standard of living, i.e. butter, eggs, milk, etc., it would probably cost him $700 or more per month. That would be the true H.C.L. for this family.
Take the motor car owners and the cost of running their cars. Gasoline used to be $1.10 per gallon, and now $2.60 per gallon. High cost of running (H.C.L.) increased $1.50 or 135 per cent. Your H.C.L. allowance is only 50 per cent: you are short of 85 per cent., therefore you cannot afford to buy gasoline, so buy a substitute and run your car on kerosene and record and inform Miss Hinder that kerosene has increased 10 cents. Poor engine, how it will suffer.
Poor children, they have not had milk for months now.
P.F. 30.
Shanghai, Feb. 14.
pages.zh:
生活费用指数（H. C. L.）调查：
现行方法受到批评
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——我今日致函阁下，特别是致信欣德小姐（Miss Hinder），其目的仅如下文所述。出于各种原因，我希望欣德小姐及其工作人员尊重我的身份，因为通过她的档案可以追踪到我的身份。

据我了解，欣德小姐在努力得出并编制显示外侨生活费用指数（H.C.L.）的统计数据方面，并未获得社区的支持。此前，工部局在收到许多公司询问是否有显示外侨生活费用指数的数据后，将此项工作交由能干的欣德小姐负责。

遗憾的是，欣德小姐未能获得上海社区的支持，因为我们（如果我可以这样说的话）外侨社区中的工薪阶层，将从确立真实的外侨生活费用指数中获益良多。

那么，为什么，为什么会缺乏这种支持呢？显然，某些地方出了问题，或者也许我应该说，家庭主妇们在按照欣德小姐的要求遵守现行记录保存制度时遇到了不便和麻烦，更不用说下班回家的丈夫们所面临的神经紧张和易怒情绪了。例如，我的妻子在第一个月就没有完成她的记录，那个月结束时，她非常慷慨地让我享受了自己做这些记录的“乐趣”。她在厨师问题上遇到了无尽的麻烦，而且她不想因为换掉他而再找一个同样糟糕甚至更糟的厨师。

大多数靠预算生活的家庭，每天给厨师固定的买菜钱，而众所周知，厨师们讨厌被盘问。他们必须进行惯常的克扣，如果你换了厨师，情况又会重演。因此，如果你对他端上桌的饭菜质量和数量感到满意，你宁愿放弃保存这些记录，也不愿让他一走了之。

为什么要让几百名家庭主妇写下同样的东西呢？例如，她们上周为某种品牌的黄油每磅支付 5.50 美元，本周支付 5.60 美元；昨天的牛肉多少钱，今天的牛肉多少钱，等等，等等。这些细节可以从你们每日发布当前市场价格的报纸上获得，欣德小姐也可以从几家主要及其他商店店主那里获得当前的食品杂货价格。

在我看来，欣德小姐是在“找错对象”（barking up the wrong tree）。让我们假设一个养家糊口的人月薪为 400 美元，几年没有加薪，也没有领取任何生活费用津贴。他的生活成本并没有增加。他能够住在漂亮的房子或公寓里，买得起黄油、鸡蛋、牛奶和优质牛肉等。现在，既然一个人必须量入为出，即依靠 400 美元生活，他和他的家人被迫住在一间房的公寓里，吃人造黄油代替黄油，孩子们没有鸡蛋，没有牛奶，吃着劣质牛肉，而他的妻子为欣德小姐保存记录，显示人造黄油在一周内上涨了 20 美分。这能告诉欣德小姐他的生活费用指数吗？不能，因为他的生活费用并没有上涨。真正发生的是，他的生活水平急剧下降，而要维持他原来的生活水平，即食用黄油、鸡蛋、牛奶等，每月可能需要花费 700 美元或更多。那才是这个家庭真实的生活费用指数。

再以汽车车主及其用车成本为例。汽油以前是每加仑 1.10 美元，现在是每加仑 2.60 美元。高昂的运行成本（H.C.L.）增加了 1.50 美元，即 135%。你的生活费用津贴只有 50%：你还短缺 85%，因此你买不起汽油，所以购买替代品，用煤油开车，并记录并告知欣德小姐煤油上涨了 10 美分。可怜的引擎，它将遭受怎样的折磨。

可怜的孩子们，他们已经好几个月没有喝牛奶了。
P.F. 30.
上海，2 月 14 日。

FEB 1 6 1940

Flour And Wheat

The price of second-grade products was still being quoted at $10.00 in cash yesterday to local buyers. The mills, however, offered only a few hundred bags with respect to the high price of wheat so that the unofficial market registered new highs with "Gun Cart" flour advancing to $15.40, and "Red Wealthy God" brand improving to $13.00 per bag. North China dealers absorbed 10,000 bags of "Red Wealthy God" flour.
The rate of native wheat hit a new record yesterday with Soochow wheat being sold at $25 per bag or $3 high as compared with the previous close. On account of the high rates the Fooh Sing and the Fooh Foong flour mills were not in the market while local dealers bought 12 carloads of Soochow wheat.

1940 年 2 月 16 日

面粉与小麦

昨日，二等产品的现金报价仍为每袋 10.00 美元，面向本地买家。然而，由于小麦价格高企，面粉厂仅提供了数百袋，导致非官方市场创下新高，“枪车”牌面粉涨至每袋 15.40 美元，“红财神”牌改善至每袋 13.00 美元。华北商人吸收了 10,000 袋“红财神”牌面粉。

昨日，国产小麦汇率创下新纪录，苏州小麦以每袋 25 美元的价格售出，比前一收盘价高出 3 美元。由于汇率高企，福兴（Fooh Sing）和福丰（Fooh Foong）面粉厂未入市交易，而本地商人购买了 12 车皮苏州小麦。

CHINA PRESS

FEB 1 O 1940

Municipal Officials In
Both Areas Urged
To Halt Profiteering

Municipal authorities in the
Settlement and Concession have
been petitioned to put an immediate
halt to the activities of profiteers
and speculators in the local com-
modity market, it was learned yes-
terday.

The petitions were submitted
by the First Special District
Citizens' Federation, a Chinese
residents' organization in the
Settlement A letter with
similar contents was also ad-
dressed to the Chinese Cham-
ber of Commerce.

Consideration Promised

While official comment could not
be obtained yesterday, an official of
the Council told THE CHINA PRESS
that due consideration would be
given the petitions when they
reached the responsible quarters.

The Federation's petition to the
foreign Municipal Councils urged
that measures be taken to fix a
maximum price for coal as had been
done for rice, in view of the soaring
prices of fuel in Shanghai.

It was further requested that in-
vestigation be carried on to
ascertain the amount of coal now
stored in Shanghai, that profiteers
be punished and that importation
of coal be encouraged through
efforts of the two Councils.

In the Federation's petition
to the Chamber, it was propos-
ed that a committee for the
stabilization of commodity
prices be immediately establi-
shed, a similar proposal, it was
stated, having been submitted
to the Chamber several months
ago.

The letter stated that the people's
living cost had now reached a very
critical stage owing to the unbat-
ted rise of commodity prices and
asked the Chamber to negotiate
with the Settlement and Concession
authorities for the immediate est-
ablishment of the proposed com-
mittee "in order to deliver the
public from their present precarious
position"

《大美晚报》

1940 年 2 月 10 日

敦促两租界市政当局
制止牟取暴利

据悉，昨日有人请愿要求公共租界和法租界的市政当局立即制止当地商品市场上牟取暴利的商人和投机者的活动。

这些请愿书由第一特区市民联合会提交，该组织是公共租界内的中国居民组织。一封内容相似的信件也致送给了上海总商会。

承诺予以考虑

虽然昨日未能获得官方评论，但工部局的一位官员告诉《大美晚报》，当请愿书送达主管部门时，将给予充分考虑。

联合会在致外国市政当局的请愿书中敦促采取措施，鉴于上海燃料价格飞涨，应像对大米那样规定煤炭的最高限价。

此外，还要求进行调查，以确定上海目前的煤炭储量，惩罚牟取暴利者，并通过两个工部局的努力鼓励煤炭进口。

在联合会致商会的请愿书中，提议立即成立一个稳定物价委员会，据称，类似的提议已在几个月前提交给商会。

信中指出，由于商品价格毫无节制地上涨，人民的生活成本已达到非常危急的阶段，并要求商会与公共租界和法租界当局谈判，立即成立拟议中的委员会，“以使公众摆脱目前的危险境地”

Dishonest Dealers Warned As
Rice Prices Soar Higher

Drastic police action against
rice dealers selling at prices
above the limits set by
Settlement and Concession
authorities will be taken
beginning today as prices of rice
reached the unprecedented high
of $54 per picul when the
market closed yesterday after-
noon.

Proclaimed under the joint aus-
pices of the Concession and the
Settlement, the prices of domestic
rice, including kan rice and sien
rice, were fixed at $40 and $32 per
picul respectively.

Despite the joint proclamation,
rice merchants in Shanghai for
many days, especially as the spring
festival approached, had been sell-
ing domestic rice at far above the
fixed limits.

Sales Not Recorded

Although no sales had been
recorded at the official city
markets for several weeks, con-
sumers reported they had to
pay the excessive prices at all
rice shops if they desired to
purchase domestic rice.

Reports reaching THE CHINA
PRESS last night stated that even
sien rice, their consumers be-
ing the poorest class of Chin-
ese residents here, was quoted at
as high as $40 per picul, or $8
in excess of the official limits.

While Saigon rice was reported ar-
riving in the city in huge quantities,
dealers stated yesterday afternoon
that the arrivals would in no way
help to keep the prices down in
view of the constantly mounting
freight charges due principally to a
shortage of bottoms for transporta-
tion.

All-Time High Reached

Quotations for Saigon rice

reached the all-time high of
$55 per picul, and trading
quarters were of the opinion
that they might hit the $60
mark in the not distant future.
No relief was in sight, it was
stated.

Arrivals of domestic rice, like-
wise, had diminished to a new
low since the approaching of
the holiday season, according to
informed quarters. Traders
were said to have found it no
easier to bring their stock to
Shanghai from the growing
areas in view of constantly in-
creasing Japanese interference.

Confiscation of domestic rice being
transported to Shanghai for non-
payment of exorbitant fees and
charges imposed by Japanese
authorities and their Chinese agents
was reported to have been frequent.

Exports Discouraged

Since recent weeks, exporters of
rice in the growing areas were
stated to have found it increasing-
ly difficult to obtain permits for
shipment of rice to Shanghai.
Dealers stated that Japanese buyers
in the occupied areas had been ex-
tremely active, their purchases being
largely consigned to Japan ap-
parently to relieve the acute short-
age there.

In view of the mounting cost of
Saigon rice and the diminishing
imports of domestic rice, informed
quarters believed it would be
extremely difficult for the Cheap
Rice Sale Committee to maintain
the old rate when the sales reopen-
ed on February 23. When the pre-
sent stock of about 40,000 bags
available for sale is exhausted, the
Committee was expected to face
great difficulty in securing new
stock for the sales at the former
prices.
pages.zh:
米价飙升，警告不法商贩

随着昨日午后收盘时米价达到每担 54 美元的前所未有的高点，从今天开始，将对以高于公共租界和法租界当局设定的限价出售大米的米商采取严厉的警务行动。

在法租界和公共租界的共同主持下宣布，国产米的价格，包括籼米和粳米，分别固定为每担 40 美元和 32 美元。

尽管有联合公告，但上海的米商在多日内，特别是随着春节临近，一直以远高于固定限价的价格出售国产米。

销售未记录

虽然官方城市市场已有数周未记录销售，但消费者报告称，如果他们想购买国产米，必须在所有米店支付过高的价格。

昨晚传给《大美晚报》的报告称，即使是主要消费者为本地最贫困中国居民的粳米，报价也高达每担 40 美元，超出官方限价 8 美元。

虽然有报道称大量西贡米运抵本市，但经销商昨日下午表示，鉴于运费不断上涨（主要是由于运输船舶短缺），到货根本无助于压低价格。

创下历史新高

西贡米的报价

达到每担 55 美元的历史最高水平，交易界人士认为，在不久的将来可能会触及 60 美元大关。据说，目前看不到缓解的迹象。

据知情人士透露，自节日季节临近以来，国产米的到货量也降至新低。据说，鉴于日本人的干扰不断增加，贸易商发现将库存从产区运往上海并不更容易。

据报道，因未支付日本当局及其中国代理人征收的高额费用和收费，运往上海的国产米被没收的情况频繁发生。

出口受阻

据称，近几周来，产区的稻米出口商发现越来越难以获得向上海装运稻米的许可证。经销商表示，占领区的日本买家一直非常活跃，他们的采购大部分运往日本，显然是为了缓解那里的严重短缺。

鉴于西贡米成本上升和国产米进口减少，知情人士认为，平价米销售委员会在 2 月 23 日重新开售时，将极难维持原有费率。当目前可供销售的约 40,000 袋库存耗尽时，预计委员会在以先前价格获取新库存方面将面临巨大困难。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
Feb 15 1919

The Rice Lines:
A Reader's Queries
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
Sir,—For how long will the
pathetic line of ragged humanity be
permitted to hang around the rice
shops for hours on end just to get
their $1's worth of cheaper rice?
And when this comes to an end,
what then? Some months back I
foolishly thought that the authori-
ties had at last decided to take some
drastic steps to keep the price of
rice down. But no—the price is still
mounting and the poor are still
getting poorer. Perhaps the pivot
boys do not care about the price of
rice, but I cannot believe that they
do not know about it. Surely their
servants eat rice! Or do these ser-
vants draw their wages in sterling
also?
E. M.
Shanghai, Feb. 14.

一位读者的疑问
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——那群衣衫褴褛、令人怜悯的民众，为了买到价值一元的较便宜的大米，被允许在米店周围连续徘徊数小时，这种情况还要持续多久？而当这一切结束时，又将如何？几个月前，我曾天真地以为当局终于决定采取一些严厉措施来压低米价。但事实并非如此——米价仍在攀升，穷人依旧愈发贫困。或许那些巡捕房的洋人小伙计并不在乎米价，但我无法相信他们对此一无所知。毕竟他们的仆人也吃大米！或者说，这些仆人的工资也是以英镑支付的吗？

E. M.
上海，2月14日。

FEB 1 1940

Rice Market

No official trading in white rice was
reported yesterday. The outside market,
however, advanced, and best-quality cer-
eal moved up to $50.00 per picul. The
volume of business transacted aggregated
about 3,000 piculs.

The price of foreign rice hit a new
high yesterday, with the rate of first-grade
Saigon rice improving to $50.50, repre-
senting a gain of $1.50 as compared with
the previous close. Local buyers showed
brisk demand, and the day's turnover
totaled at 20,000 bags of various kinds
of foreign cereals.

According to reliable market reports,
some of the major dealers have ordered
1,000 tons of second-grade Saigon rice at
$51.50 per bag of 220 lbs., and 600 tons
of lower-grade qualities at $44.50.

1940年2月1日

米市

昨日据报无白米官方交易。然而，场外市场价格上涨，优质粳米价格涨至每担50.00美元。成交总量约为3,000担。

昨日洋米价格创出新高，一级西贡米价格升至50.50美元，较前一交易日收盘价上涨1.50美元。本地买家需求旺盛，当日各类洋米总成交量达20,000包。

据可靠市场消息，部分大商行已以每包（220磅）51.50美元的价格订购1,000吨二级西贡米，并以44.50美元的价格订购600吨低等级米。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

NOV 20 1939

Rice Prices Begin
To Increase

Manipulators Reported Busy,
But Big Supplies Due

Despite the fact that prices of
various grades of rice have in-
creased during the past few days
after following a downward trend
for some time, Chinese press re-
ports indicate that Shanghai people
should not worry about the future
situation of rice here as authorities
in Saigon have lifted the rice em-
bargo. Already, Shanghai rice mer-
chants are said to have successfully
concluded negotiations with Saigon
merchants for purchasing 500 tons
of rice.

Negotiations for the purchase of
19,000 bags of Saigon rice are also
reported to have just been con-
cluded and they are expected to
arrive here early next month. Rice
is being transported to this city by
merchants making purchases in the
occupied interior despite transporta-
tion difficulties. In the next few
days, large quantities of the grain
are expected to arrive for storage.

Chinese bankers here are said to
be very careful in granting loans
to rice merchants who want to buy
rice for storage purposes because
they want to prevent manipulators
from preying upon the public. Un-
less rice merchants applying for
credits are guaranteed by execu-
tives of public bodies to which they
belong, Chinese banks will not con-
sider their applications, it is stated.

A review of the commercial sec-
tions of the Chinese press yester-
day revealed that manipulators were
again active on Saturday in the rice
market. According to the "Shun
Pao," the manipulators increased
their prices by $3 or $4 per picul
explaining that by doing so rice
merchants in the interior will be
more willing to transport their cargo
to Shanghai.

《字林西报》。

1939年11月20日

米价开始
上涨

据报道投机商活动频繁，
但大批供应即将抵达

尽管各类大米的价格在经历了一段时间的下跌趋势后，于过去几天内有所上涨，但中文报纸的报道指出，上海市民不必担心本地未来的大米局势，因为西贡当局已解除大米禁运令。据说，上海米商已成功与西贡商人达成谈判，购买500吨大米。

据报道，购买19,000袋西贡大米的谈判也刚刚结束，预计这批大米将于下月初抵达此处。尽管运输困难，商人们仍从被占领的内地采购并将大米运至本市。预计在未来几天内，将有大量谷物运抵储存。

据悉，本地中国银行家在向希望购米储存的米商发放贷款时非常谨慎，因为他们希望防止投机商掠夺公众利益。据称，除非申请信贷的米商能得到其所属公共团体高管的担保，否则中国银行将不考虑其申请。

回顾昨日中文报纸的商业版块发现，投机商周六再次在大米市场活跃。据《申报》报道，投机商将每担价格提高了3或4美元，并解释称这样做会使内地米商更愿意将货物运往上海。

CHINA PRESS.

NOV 20 1939

Cost Of Rice
Increases $4
Over Weekend

Speculators in the rice market yesterday were believed to be running amuck again as the price of the grain registered a $4 increase over the week-end. Traders revealed last night that this was the largest gain at any one time since the price began to drop from the $42-per-picul mark early three months ago.

A grain dealer asserted last night that no explanation could be offered for the mounting cost of rice at this time. He stated that imports from the occupied areas for the past two months had averaged about 6,000 bags per day this being only slightly below the amount consumed here daily.

It was further pointed out that since all producing areas reported bumper crops this year, a steady inflow of the grain to the foreign areas was regarded as certain, especially in view of the fact that the export of rice from the producing areas had not been banned.

A special meeting of leading Chinese rice merchants was called yesterday to discuss ways and means of remedying the present situation. It was resolved that the committee set up to regulate price among members of the rice guild should continue to persuade dealers to refrain from wild speculation.

Dealers close to the rice market indicated that although 6,000 bags of rice were known to have arrived in Shanghai almost daily, the amount traded at the market had averaged less than 2,000 bags daily for the past three months. This means, it was pointed out, that at least 4,000 bags arriving here daily is used as subject of speculation.

Official action to control speculation was expected in trading cities if the present price hikes continued to maintain their pace.

（批：Like (30/11)）

《大美晚报》。

1939年11月20日

周末米价
上涨4美元

据信，昨日大米市场的投机商再次肆意妄为，导致该谷物价格在周末上涨了4美元。交易商昨晚透露，这是自三个月前价格开始从每担42美元的水平下跌以来，单次最大涨幅。

一位粮食经销商昨晚断言，目前无法解释大米成本上升的原因。他表示，过去两个月从被占领区进口的大米平均每天约为6,000袋，仅略低于本地每日消耗量。

此外还指出，鉴于所有产区今年均报告丰收，谷物稳定流入租界地区被视为必然之事，特别是考虑到产区并未禁止大米出口这一事实。

昨日召开了主要华商米业会议，讨论补救当前局势的方法。会议决议，负责调节米业公会成员价格的委员会应继续劝说经销商避免疯狂投机。

接近大米市场的交易商表示，虽然已知每天有近6,000袋大米抵达上海，但在过去三个月里，市场日均交易量不足2,000袋。这意味着，据指出，每天抵达这里的至少4,000袋大米被用作投机对象。

如果目前的涨价势头持续下去，预计各贸易城市将采取官方行动来控制投机。

（批注：Like (11月30日)）

Foodstuffs Tax Collection Office established on boats
in Whangpoo River opposite Fish Market, Point
Island

It has been learned that a tax collection
office, established by Japanese and Chinese with
offices on a boat and a steam launch, lying in the
Whangpoo River in the vicinity of the former Fish
Market, Point Island, commenced functioning on
August 13, collecting taxes on commodities passing
that spot, according to the following scale :-
Rice : $1 per bag.
Wheat: $0.30 per bag.
Bean : $0.25 per bag.
However, goods transported by foreign owned vessels
are not subject to taxation. In consequence of the
levy, it is expected that the tax will influence the
prices of these commodities in the local market.

Information has been obtained that the management
of the different local Japanese industrial concerns have
obtained the services of the families and relations of the
interpreters employed in their mills and intend despatching
them to rural districts around Shanghai for the purpose
of purchasing rice, wheat and other cereals. The capital
required for this project has been furnished by the Japanese
mills concerned and the stocks will be transported to
Shanghai for disposal. Any profits accruing from this
venture have been promised to the relations of those employees.
It is suspected that the real object behind this
plan is a monopoly on all cereals coming from the districts
that supply Shanghai, although it is given out by the
Japanese concerned that they want to safeguard the supplies
for workers in their employ.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
SPECIAL BRANCH
................
INTELLIGENCE REPORT      May 18, 1938.

Miscellaneous

Chinese delegate to the International Labour Conference
leaves Shanghai

Mr. Ling Kong-hou ( 林康侯 ),secretary of the
Chinese Bankers' Association, 59 Hongkong Road, who has
been appointed employers' delegate to the forthcoming
International Labour Conference at Geneva, left Shanghai
for Europe by the s.s. "Conte Biancamano" at 8.30 a.m.
May 18. A party of Chinese notables in Shanghai numbering
about thirty attended the Customs Jetty, The Bund, on his
departure.

Food hawkers in French Concession

A number of food hawkers in Nantao, as a result of
the hostilities, removed to the French Concession and
have been conducting their business in Rue Colbert. As
no permission had been obtained from the French Police
to use that street, the Police commenced removing the
hawkers from that thoroughfare on May 1. On the morning
of May 17, ten representatives of the hawkers called at
the French Municipal Council, where they submitted an
appeal for the cancellation of the order, but their request
was not entertained.

It is reported that these representatives intend
visiting the offices of Butterfield & Swire, The French
Bund, to-day, May 18, which are situated at the mouth of
Rue Colbert, for the purpose of enlisting their support
in persuading the Council to desist from their removal.

杂项

出席国际劳工大会的中国代表离开上海

中国银行公会秘书林康侯先生，地址香港路59号，已被任命为即将在日内瓦举行的国际劳工大会的雇主代表，于5月18日上午8时30分乘坐“孔泰·比安卡马诺”号（s.s. "Conte Biancamano"）轮船离开上海前往欧洲。约三十名上海中国名流组成的送行团体在外滩海关码头为其送行。

法租界内的食品小贩

南市的一些食品小贩因战事迁至法租界，并在科尔贝路（Rue Colbert）经营生意。由于未获得法国警察当局使用该街道的许可，警方于5月1日开始将该街道上的小贩驱离。5月17日上午，十名小贩代表前往法国公董局，提交撤销该命令的申诉，但其请求未被受理。

据报道，这些代表打算于今日，即5月18日，前往位于科尔贝路路口的太古洋行（Butterfield & Swire）办事处，以期争取其支持，劝说公董局停止驱逐行动。

Date April 23, 1938.

Subject General increase in prices of local foodstuffs - expected.

Made by ............ and ............ Forwarded by Inspector Payn.

Further enquiries indicate that the Japanese
Military Authorities have decided to modify some of the
portentious features of their original scheme aiming to
control the supply of foodstuffs in the Settlement and the
French Concession as well as in the regions around Shanghai.
According to later reports, they have resolved to abandon
their intention of putting "military notes" into circulation
among farmers in the Japanese controlled areas. In
substitution, they are now planning to raise funds through
effective control of rice.

By gradually increasing the price of rice,
they aim to hit the Chinese population of the foreign areas
at their weakest spot - the rice bowl. It seems, however,
that the underlying object of the present scheme is to prevail
upon the many thousand refugees of middle and low classes in
foreign areas that Shanghai is no place for them to make
a peaceful living because of the high price of foodstuffs,
so that they may be forced to go back to their home towns
and villages and again to engage in productive work.

进一步调查显示，日本军方当局决定修改其原计划中一些旨在控制公共租界、法租界以及上海周边地区食品供应的严峻措施。根据后续报告，他们已决定放弃在日本控制区向农民流通“军用手票”的意图。作为替代，他们现在计划通过对大米的有效控制来筹集资金。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
C.S.6, Special Branch Station 8039A
SECRET REPORT 324 38
Date April 21, 1938.

Subject General increase in prices of local foodstuffs to be expected.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Rapp

Despite the fact that the Japanese Military
Authorities are already exacting heavy fees from importers
of food products in Japanese occupied areas, the local food
situation is not considered to be serious at present. It
is learned, however, that the Japanese Military Authorities
have recently decided to enforce still stricter control over
the trade in local foodstuffs. This measure is designed to
tighten their grip over the Settlement and the French
Concession and also to starve into submission the Chinese
population in these areas. It is impossible to make a fore-
cast as to what extent Japanese ambitions will be successful
but in order to further their plans, the Headquarters of the
Japanese Military Garrison will soon establish a special
control bureau, which will centralize all importations of rice,
livestock, wheat, vegetables etc. into Shanghai.

Local importers will be required to apply for
special permits from this bureau. When applying for such
permits, they will be required to specify the kind of goods
to be imported, the amount to be purchased, the place of origin
and date of importation and the name of steamer to carry the
cargo. It is reported that the fee to be paid for the
permits is approximately 30% of the value of the goods im-
ported.

The new regulations include a measure according
to which all local importers will be required to exchange
legal tender notes for Japanese "Military Notes" (軍用票)
and to buy rice and other foodstuffs with latter notes in the
Japanese controlled areas for importation into Shanghai.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 21 APR. 1938 mB.）

日期 1938年4月21日。

主题 预计本地食品价格普遍上涨。

由拉普（Rapp）督察制作并转呈

尽管日本军方当局已经在日军占领区向食品进口商征收高额费用，但目前的本地食品局势尚不被认为严重。然而获悉，日本军方当局最近决定对本地食品贸易实施更严格的控制。此举旨在加强对公共租界和法租界的掌控，并试图通过饥饿迫使这些区域的中国民众屈服。无法预测日本方面的野心能在多大程度上得逞，但为了推进其计划，日本驻屯军司令部不久将设立一个特别管制局，集中管理所有进入上海的大米、牲畜、小麦、蔬菜等进口物资。

本地进口商将被要求向该局申请特别许可证。在申请此类许可证时，他们需注明进口货物的种类、购买数量、原产地、进口日期以及承运货物的轮船名称。据报道，许可证的费用约为进口货物价值的30%。

新规定包括一项措施，要求所有本地进口商将法定货币兑换为日本“军用手票”（軍用票），并在日本控制区使用后者购买大米和其他食品，以便进口到上海。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科 1938年4月21日 mB.）

Enforcement of this measure will result in increased

to be another measure designed by the Japanese Military
Authorities to replace legal tender notes with their military
